source: FAO Synopsis of biological data on yellowfin tuna, Table I; values are proportions of fork length for specimens from the northwestern Caribbean

secondDorsalLength.note: increases strongly with size; do not use one fixed adult value

analLength.note: increases strongly with size; do not use one fixed adult value

meristics.firstDorsalSpines: typically 14 in cited sample; broader modern diagnosis 11-14

colorAndSurface.ventrolateralPattern: oblique or near-vertical broken pale lines and dots
colorAndSurface.pectoral: inner side dark; outer side greyish or yellowish

usageRule: These are calibration bounds, not a replacement for copying FISH-REF-002. Any source-copy dimension outside a stable biological range must be flagged as a source-vs-species conflict before improvement is attempted.
